claim.purpose: Correct mergeability-state classification without widening merge authority

initial.title: [v0.91.8][csdlc-v2][tooling] Preserve blocked and unstable PR mergeability states
initial.goal: Make csdlc-pr-state distinguish stale-base ancestry from pending GitHub merge-policy states.
initial.required_outcome: Explicit mergeability classification preserves behind as stale_base, blocked and unstable as waiting, dirty as conflicted, and unknown as waiting with focused proof.
authority_boundary: Issue 5695 owns mergeability classification and focused tests only
csdlc-merge remains fail-closed and GitHub remains merge authority
initial.task_boundary: Repair the bounded mergeability mapping and prove its state table before execution.
acceptance_criteria: AC-1: Every supported mergeability variant has an explicit classification
AC-2: blocked and unstable cannot be reported as stale_base
AC-3: behind remains stale_base and dirty remains conflicted
AC-4: Focused tests prove the table and csdlc-merge remains fail-closed until clean ancestry and required checks are observed
dependencies: Existing csdlc-pr-state classification and merge gate tests
non_goals: No provider, Runtime, AWS, or CI workflow changes
initial.plan_summary: Read the current octocrab state mapping, implement an explicit classification table, add focused state coverage, validate the touched crate, obtain exact review, and publish only after review.

steps.action: Bind issue 5695 with disjoint source and card paths
Replace wildcard mergeability fallback with explicit pending-state mapping
Add focused tests for every supported mergeability variant and merge fail-closed behavior
Run focused validation and exact review before publication

invariants: blocked and unstable are pending rather than stale
Merge eligibility still requires required checks and review
risks: octocrab may add a new enum variant
classification tests can omit a state
pending states can be mistaken for merge eligibility
stop_conditions: The enum variants cannot be verified from the pinned dependency
The change requires merge-authority policy changes
Work would touch provider, Runtime, AWS, or unrelated CI surfaces

validation_lanes.proof_role: Exercise explicit mergeability-state classification and fail-closed merge predicates
Verify formatting and strict lint for the touched Rust source
Verify the bounded diff has no whitespace corruption

initial.failure_policy: Fail closed on unclassified variants, stale-base misclassification, merge-gate weakening, scope drift, or failed focused validation.
review_prompts: Does every supported octocrab MergeableState map explicitly?
Can blocked or unstable ever become stale_base?
Does csdlc-merge remain fail-closed while checks or ancestry are pending?
